nodes.label: object_repair.py (Object-Only Pixel Restore)
nodes.rationale: Restores only a damaged object's pixels from the original while preserving the dub's lip-sync; invariants (NCC tracking anchored to Claude-vision keyframes, damage-based mouth-protection gate, temporal smoothing) were each earned by a real observed failure such as tracker drift and interpolated lips.

nodes.label: Wav2Lip (Local Lip-Sync)
nodes.rationale: Stock inference.py aborted on face-less frames (product end-cards); patched locally to reuse the nearest detection, raising only if no frame has a face.

nodes.label: ComfyUI + SD1.5 (Brand Imagery Generation)
nodes.rationale: Runs --lowvram on a 4 GB RTX 3050 Ti; portable build shipped cu130 torch and was downgraded to cu126. SD1.5 cannot render text at this VRAM, so the model never draws brand text — text is composited deterministically instead.

nodes.label: faster-whisper (CUDA Transcription)
nodes.rationale: Word alignment crashes (IndexError in find_alignment) on XTTS silence; caption.py retries and falls back to segment-level timing.

nodes.label: fal.ai (Paid Cloud Media Engines)
nodes.rationale: Paid engines sit behind explicit cost-confirmation gates and a spend tracker; the design default is free/local engines first.

nodes.label: MiniMax Voice Clone / speech-02-hd TTS
nodes.rationale: $1.50 one-time clone per person, reusable via cached voice.json; needs >=10s reference audio; sample_rate must be an integer.

nodes.label: Headless Claude CLI (claude -p)
nodes.rationale: All LLM work (script rewriting, clone-script generation, DubSync vision advisor) uses the user's Claude subscription CLI instead of an API key; CLAUDECODE must be popped from env for nested runs.

nodes.label: Apify (Scraping Platform)
nodes.rationale: Actors change and get deprecated, so the playbook mandates searching the Apify store at run time for the best-maintained actor per source rather than hardcoding actor IDs; the REST API pattern is the stable layer.

nodes.label: Dub Workdir (script-swap/<stem>/ Data Structure)
nodes.rationale: The central data structure: a workdir with final.mp4 automatically appears in every tab; new features are told to create/extend workdirs rather than invent new storage, and stage caching in the workdir makes jobs resumable without re-running paid stages.

nodes.label: Frame-Count Integrity Rule
nodes.rationale: ffmpeg -shortest silently dropped trailing frames (660 to 657), so it is banned project-wide; encoders use -frames:v N, readers die loudly on early EOF, and every engine ffprobe-verifies output frame count equals input, deleting the take on mismatch.

nodes.label: Cost-Confirmation Money Gate + Spend Tracker
nodes.rationale: Any fal.ai action requires confirm_cost: true in the request body; run_dub_job appends estimated cost to a running total, and cloud dubs are deliberately excluded from blind resume so money is never spent without explicit confirmation.

nodes.label: GPU Lock / Cross-App Arbitration
nodes.rationale: One GPU job at a time on the 4 GB RTX 3050 Ti: concurrent XTTS/Wav2Lip runs OOM the card and all fail, so the 409 guard and cross-app lock file are load-bearing.

nodes.label: Clone Winner Feature (Ad Variant Factory)
nodes.rationale: Mass-produces variants of a proven ad keeping structure/angle/claims with fresh wording; same-actor fal runs copy voice.json to skip the $1.50 re-clone fee, and clone endpoints call engine scripts directly with --name to bypass the server's upload-derived stem.

nodes.label: DubSync Repair Suite
nodes.rationale: Fixes finished dubs without paying for a re-dub; every repair writes a take (repair-*.mp4) and never overwrites final.mp4 until promoted, so a bad repair can never destroy the deliverable.

nodes.label: Brand Studio (Static Image Ads)
nodes.rationale: Because SD1.5 on 4 GB VRAM cannot render text, the model only generates imagery; all brand text and the locked liitt wordmark PNG are overlaid deterministically with Pillow using brand-kit tokens, hard-failing on missing tokens rather than silently substituting.

nodes.label: Velocity Truth Signal (24-72h Acceleration)
nodes.rationale: Bloodhound's evidence standard: engagement/share acceleration in the last 24-72h with numbers, timeframe, and source; durable-looking signals are handed to prospector for longevity validation instead of being banked as velocity finds.

nodes.label: Longevity Truth Signal (30+ Days of Spend)
nodes.rationale: An ad still running after 30+ days of spend is proven while a viral one-day spike is noise; on Meta, which shows no US engagement numbers, longevity plus variant count IS the winner metric because advertisers only keep feeding what converts.
nodes.norm_label: longevity truth signal (30+ days of spend)

nodes.label: trend_jack Class + expires Field
nodes.rationale: Bloodhound entries share prospector's bank schemas verbatim plus exactly two markers (class trend_jack, ISO expires date +7 to +14 days) so perishable trend intelligence coexists with proven entries; prospector Mode 5 sweeps expired entries to status killed — bloodhound never deletes.

nodes.label: 'Their Why' Identity Inversion
nodes.rationale: People don't buy the brand's why; they buy their own — who they are and hope to become. Value props are phrased as identity statements, ingredients are reasons-to-believe not reasons-to-buy.

nodes.label: Identity Ladder
nodes.rationale: Who the avatar is today, who they hope to become, and what buying the product says about them to themselves and others; every downstream deliverable must trace back to it (no orphan aesthetics).

nodes.label: Brand World (Enterable Identity)
nodes.rationale: The strongest DTC identities are enterable places/states, not slogans: they give every asset a consistent fictional container, convert purchase into entry (belonging mechanics), and extend infinitely since new products are new rooms in the same world.

nodes.label: Mascot Theory (Barry Rule)
nodes.rationale: Playful edge with a premium floor: mascots are ownable (competitors can copy a palette overnight but not accumulated character meaning) and enable cheap creative variation; the premium guardrail must always be written down.

nodes.label: Channel Sequencing (Gruns Arc)
nodes.rationale: DTC + email first to prove the identity converts, retail second, broadcast third — mass media amplifies distribution that already exists; buying broadcast before DTC proof is an anti-pattern.

nodes.label: Primitive/Semantic Token Split
nodes.rationale: Two-layer token architecture so sibling brands re-theme by swapping semantic mappings while keeping components; exactly one action color because if everything pops nothing converts; this split is why Gruns sub-universes could extend without rebranding.

nodes.label: 5 Levels of Awareness (Eugene Schwartz)
nodes.rationale: Classify the target avatar, not the market average; one ad = one awareness level, and the entry level must be stated on every angle bank entry so the scriptwriter knows where the ad opens.

nodes.label: 5 Stages of Market Sophistication (Schwartz)
nodes.rationale: Determines which claim types are dead; if 3+ competitors use the same mechanism it's burnt. Stage 5 (total skepticism) is where identity/brand-world/mascot plays win — the Gruns move.

nodes.label: Kell VSL Beat Structure
nodes.rationale: Shared beat map (Hook, Lead/Big Promise, Mechanism/Story, Proof stack, Offer, CTA) that winner teardowns are mapped onto so the scriptwriter can transplant patterns directly.

nodes.label: Voice-of-Customer Mining Method
nodes.rationale: Verbatim over paraphrase: 1-star competitor reviews are angle ammunition, 5-star reviews reveal the desired end state; customer language is the product and is never laundered into marketing-speak.

nodes.label: Bank Entry Status Lifecycle (untested-testing-proven-killed)
nodes.rationale: Only prospector Mode 4/5 or explicit human input changes status; scripts cite bank ids in frontmatter so ad results flow back to promote or kill entries — this closed loop is what makes the banks compound instead of rot.

nodes.label: Cardinal Rule: Stop for Transcript Edit
nodes.rationale: Always stop and hand the transcript to the user before generating any voice or lip-sync — the whole point is swapping in new marketing copy, so rendering the original words wastes money and defeats the purpose; clone may run in parallel since it doesn't depend on the script.
nodes.norm_label: cardinal rule: stop for transcript edit

nodes.label: Gruns Case Study
nodes.rationale: Raindrop partnered at Seed stage, built strategy/identity/mascot/performance creative; launched gummies Aug 2023, sold to Unilever for ~$1.2B in under three years — the evidence base for the whole method.

nodes.label: House Upsell Formulas (Warning Stock-Up, Appreciation Bonus)
nodes.rationale: Post-purchase scripts continue a purchase in progress: never make the buyer re-decide, one offer per video, price stated once anchored to the cart, and every unverifiable claim goes in a FLAGS list rather than being invented.
nodes.norm_label: house upsell formulas (warning stock-up, appreciation bonus)

nodes.label: Creator Page (video-to-new-ad pipeline UI)
nodes.rationale: Turns existing videos into new ads via a gated 4-step flow (clean subtitles -> new script -> dub -> result); nothing advances until the user approves each step, protecting source footage and paid spend. Calls /api/creator/library, /api/creator/meta, /api/script, /api/copywrite, /api/clean-subs, /api/clean-restore, /api/run (transcribe/dub/caption), /api/qc/ai-review, /api/edit, /api/upload, /api/jobs, /api/chat, /api/agent-note.

nodes.label: Dubbing Studio Page
nodes.rationale: Clone the voice, swap the words, re-lip-sync. 3-step flow (transcribe -> new script -> dub) with a local/free engine (XTTS v2 + Wav2Lip) vs cloud/paid engine (fal.ai F5/MiniMax voice + LatentSync/MuseTalk/VEED/sync v2 lips). Calls /api/overview, /api/script, /api/run, /api/job, /api/upload; parses '=== stage: X ===' job log lines into a 3-box progress UI.

nodes.label: Subtitle Eraser Page
nodes.rationale: One-button burned-in caption removal: finds captions automatically, AI-reconstructs the background (no blur, no black box), shows a before/after comparison. Calls /api/qc/videos, /api/qc/remove-subs (method=erase), /api/job, /api/upload; progress parser tracks scan -> AI chunk inpainting -> encode phases and detects the ProPainter engine vs a classic-inpaint blur fallback.

nodes.rationale: Full production desk: products & scripts rail, 'Build a VSL' (Claude writes the package from a product + script + research docs), research banks browser, video library with a stackable ffmpeg editor (trim/zoom/speed/text/volume/join), inspector (ffprobe), job activity, trash, and fal.ai spend breakdown. Calls /api/overview, /api/product, /api/build-vsl, /api/run, /api/bank, /api/file, /api/edit, /api/concat, /api/qc/probe, /api/output-*, /api/trash, /api/jobs, /api/spend, /api/chat.
nodes.norm_label: mission control page (vsl auto production desk)

nodes.label: Quality Control Page
nodes.rationale: Human + AI review station: model scoreboard, frame-stepping player (0.25x/0.5x speed, 3s loop, comma/period frame keys) for lip-sync checks, tech-spec probe with warnings, AI review scores, 4-item manual checklist (lip_sync/dubbing/quality/realism) with pass/fail verdicts, and subtitle-removal tools (auto erase, draw-box erase/blur, crop, strip embedded tracks). Calls /api/qc/videos, /api/qc/models, /api/qc/probe, /api/qc/frames, /api/qc/review, /api/qc/ai-review, /api/qc/remove-subs, /api/job.

nodes.label: ComfyUI Studio Page (local image tools)
nodes.rationale: Free local-GPU image tools in 4 tabs: generate (SD 1.5 DreamShaper, brand presets), 4x Real-ESRGAN upscale, inpaint (mask repaint), ControlNet keyframe. Calls /api/studio/brand, /api/studio/upload, /api/studio/run. Warns ControlNet is slow on 4 GB VRAM (use run_nvidia_lowvram.bat).

nodes.label: Subtitles Studio Page
nodes.rationale: Erase burned-in subs -> burn new word-timed captions -> edit any caption line and fast re-burn (plus Claude '/api/aifix' proofreading). Deliberately splits work across two engines: erase/restore on this server's proven pipeline (width-16 ProPainter fix, auto-detect, corruption retry) via /api/clean-subs; captions/AI-fix on the merged 5180 engine proxied at /subs. Same data root; jobs merged from both /api/jobs endpoints and stopped on the engine that owns them.

nodes.label: autoVSL Dashboard REST API
nodes.rationale: The shared backend contract all dashboard pages poll: job model (/api/run -> job_id, /api/job/<id>?offset= incremental log lines + status + cost, /api/job/<id>/stop), library/overview endpoints, upload, media serving under /media/, and per-run fal.ai cost reporting ({free, this_run, total}).

nodes.label: Explicit Cost-Approval Gate for Paid Runs
nodes.rationale: Design principle repeated across Creator, Dubbing, and Mission Control: any run that spends money on fal.ai shows an itemized confirm() dialog and only proceeds with confirm_cost=true in the request body; free/local paths are labeled '$0'. A header spend badge tracks cumulative fal.ai cost so the operator always knows totals.
nodes.norm_label: explicit cost-approval gate for paid runs

nodes.label: Local Free Dubbing Pipeline (XTTS v2 + Wav2Lip)
nodes.rationale: Clones the speaker's voice and speaks the new script on the local GPU (XTTS v2), optionally lip-syncing with Wav2Lip or Wav2Lip+GFPGAN HD - no network, $0. Hybrid mode keeps the free local voice and pays only for cloud lip-sync (LatentSync), positioned as best value against full-cloud tiers.
nodes.norm_label: local free dubbing pipeline (xtts v2 + wav2lip)

nodes.label: fal.ai Cloud Generation Service
nodes.rationale: Paid cloud provider used for TTS voice (F5 zero-shot, MiniMax turbo/HD with $1.50 one-time clone), lip-sync (LatentSync/MuseTalk ~$0.20/40s, VEED ~$0.40/min, sync v2 ~$3/min, sync v2 PRO), and video shot generation (Wan 2.2, Seedance, Hailuo, Kling). Every page surfaces per-tier price labels and total spend.

nodes.label: ProPainter AI Subtitle Erase Engine
nodes.rationale: AI video inpainting that auto-detects burned-in captions and rebuilds the true background behind every letter, motion-matched frame by frame, in chunks (scan -> chunk inpaint -> encode). Falls back to classic inpaint/blur if the AI engine is unavailable. The 'proven' server pipeline carries a width-16 ProPainter fix and corruption retry; originals are always backed up and restorable.

nodes.label: Claude AI Video QC Review
nodes.rationale: Claude inspects 12 extracted frames (6 spread + 6 mid-speech burst) and scores mouth artifacts, realism, and quality out of 10, detects burned-in captions with their location (feeding the QC page's auto caption-band preset), and returns a verdict + fix suggestions. Explicit caveat: AI judges frames only, so lip-sync timing must still be confirmed by ear with the 0.5x loop. Runs on the Claude subscription (no API cost).

nodes.label: Model Scoreboard (which model combos to trust)
nodes.rationale: Aggregates AI review scores and manual pass/fail verdicts per model combo (via /api/qc/models) so the operator learns which voice+lipsync model combinations actually perform - a local feedback loop over generation quality.
nodes.norm_label: model scoreboard (which model combos to trust)

nodes.label: Research & Brand Agent (in-dashboard Claude chat)
nodes.rationale: Chat strategist embedded in Creator and Mission Control that knows the banks, research and brand; used for fresh hooks/angles/niches and teachable via a 'Teach - save to agent memory' pin (/api/agent-note). Sessions run through /api/chat with model=opus, mode=research, polled event streams.

nodes.label: Claude Brand-Aware Script Rewriter
nodes.rationale: The /api/copywrite endpoint: every rewrite feeds Claude the full research (bank hooks & angles, brand offer, ad-conversion rules) plus the video's measured speaking pace. The fit meter computes the original speaker's words/sec from transcript length / video duration so the rewritten script fills the same runtime for clean lip-sync (target 90-105% of original word count).

nodes.label: liitt / Fairy Flame Brand Kit (banks/liitt-brand-kit.json)
nodes.rationale: Brand presets (The Glow brand platform + angle bank) served by /api/studio/brand: prompt presets, a style_suffix (editorial mystic, indigo/gold Glow palette) and a brand negative_prompt auto-appended to image generation prompts.

nodes.label: autoVSL Agent System Map (AGENTS.md)
nodes.rationale: Declares the project a multi-agent ad factory: five skills chained research -> write -> produce. Agents never call each other directly - they hand off through files (banks/, research/, products/<slug>/, framework/, scripts/, output/), keeping each agent independently runnable and auditable.

nodes.label: Prospector Agent (research by longevity)
nodes.rationale: Researches proven winners (30+ days of spend), competitor teardowns, and customer language from ad libraries and reviews (web/Apify); writes banks/ and research/ reports. Its Modes 4/5 are the only writers allowed to change bank entry status.

nodes.label: Bloodhound Agent (research by velocity)
nodes.rationale: Tracks what is trending NOW (sounds, formats, memes, cultural moments) - perishable and dated; writes expiry-dated trend_jack bank entries and research/trends/ reports. Complements prospector's durable research with fresh signals.

nodes.label: Brand Platform Builder Agent
nodes.rationale: Builds brand identity, voice, positioning, naming, mascot, and avatar from a product brief; runs once per product so the writer pulls tone from it.

nodes.label: VSL Writer Agent (copywriter skill)
nodes.rationale: Turns research + brand voice into scripts, avatars, angles, and shot lists via the staged framework (intake -> avatar -> angles -> scripts -> shot list), writing products/<slug>/ scripts whose frontmatter must cite the bank ids used (no ids = unmeasurable = not finalized).

nodes.label: VSL Editor Agent (production skill)
nodes.rationale: Turns a finished script plus source/avatar footage into a finished captioned MP4 (voice-clone -> new VO -> lip-sync -> captions) using the fal.ai + ffmpeg pipeline; hard-won production rules (stop for text edit, per-video triage, fal gotchas) live in its SKILL.md.

nodes.label: banks/ Shared JSONL Data Contract
nodes.rationale: The shared JSONL banks (hooks, angles, pain-points, b-roll) that prospector and bloodhound write and the writer/editor/dashboard query; schemas in .claude/skills/prospector/references/output-schemas.md. Acts as the file-based message bus between agents.

nodes.label: DEV-README (System Architecture & Dev Handoff)
nodes.rationale: Defines the 3-layer model: ClickUp = pipeline UI, autoVSL repo = execution engine, agents = workers, with ClickUp as the message bus (no agent talks directly to another agent). Phase 1 (generation pipeline) done; Phase 2 is sync-clickup.py; custom UI deliberately deferred to Phase 4 only if ClickUp feels limiting.

nodes.label: ClickUp as Pipeline UI (7-step VSL statuses)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over a custom web UI because the team must manually add product shots, spokesperson refs, avatar intel, performance metrics and approvals - a custom UI would take weeks and duplicate ClickUp. One task = one VSL moving through 7 statuses (Research -> Hook/Angle -> Script -> Shot List -> Generating -> Review -> Live/Testing), with custom fields mapping to vsls/<slug>/ JSON.

nodes.label: Wav2Lip Lip-Sync Model
nodes.rationale: Highly accurate lip-sync for any identity, voice, language, CGI faces and synthetic voices. Trained on LRS2 at low face resolution, so lower-resolution inputs (--resize_factor) often give better results; --pads and --nosmooth exist because face-detection bounding boxes and over-smoothed detections cause chin cutoff and double-mouth artifacts.

nodes.label: Wav2Lip + GAN Model
nodes.rationale: Trade-off variant: slightly inferior lip-sync accuracy but better visual quality thanks to an additional visual-quality discriminator (~2 days training vs <1 day without).

nodes.label: A Lip Sync Expert Is All You Need (ACM MM 2020)
nodes.author: Prajwal K R, Rudrabha Mukhopadhyay, Vinay P. Namboodiri, C.V. Jawahar
nodes.norm_label: a lip sync expert is all you need (acm mm 2020)

nodes.label: Sync.so Commercial Lipsync API
nodes.rationale: Commercial hosted successor (model lipsync-2) offered because the open-source model is LRS2-licensed for non-commercial use only and the commercial version is much higher quality; accessed via syncsdk (Python) or @sync.so/sdk (TypeScript) with async job create/poll.

nodes.label: LRS2 Dataset
nodes.rationale: Training dataset for Wav2Lip; BBC copyright forbids commercial use of models trained on it, which is why the whole open-source repo is research-only.

nodes.label: Expert Lip-Sync Discriminator
nodes.rationale: Must be trained (color_syncnet_train.py) before Wav2Lip itself, per-dataset; eval loss should reach ~0.25 and Wav2Lip sync loss ~0.2 for good results — the paper's core claim is that a strong pre-trained sync expert is what makes in-the-wild lip-sync work.

nodes.label: Wav2Lip Novel Evaluation Framework
nodes.rationale: Requires no ground truth — LSE scores are computed directly from generated videos alone. A separate virtual environment is mandated for evaluation because Wav2Lip's and SyncNet's dependency versions conflict.

nodes.label: ReSyncED Real-World Lip-Sync Evaluation Dataset
nodes.rationale: Authors' own real-world benchmark, created because LRS2/LRS3/LRW filelists are BBC-copyright-restricted and lab datasets don't capture in-the-wild conditions.

Design intent: engines (subtitle-studio, autoVSL, dubbing-studio) are called in place, never copied; config.json is the single file holding every machine path; jobs are persistent, resumable and GPU-arbitrated; the original standalone apps remain untouched fallbacks.

nodes.rationale: Clones the speaker's voice and speaks the new script on the local GPU — no network, no cost; the free default against the paid fal.ai voice models.

nodes.rationale: Paid cloud alternative: F5/MiniMax voices and LatentSync (~$0.20/40s), MuseTalk, VEED (~$0.40/min), sync v2 (~$3/min), sync v2 PRO lip-sync tiers. Every UI path forces an explicit 'approve cost' confirmation before spending, and running spend is tracked and surfaced per job.

nodes.rationale: Phone-friendly remote: live job list polling /api/jobs with Stop/Resume, running/done-today/fal.ai-spend chips, quick tiles to Library, New Project, DubSync Repair, Captions, Brand Studio, Exports; Lock button hits /api/logout.

nodes.rationale: Free local GPU image tools via ComfyUI: generate (SD 1.5 DreamShaper, brand presets), 4x Real-ESRGAN upscale, inpaint (white-mask repaint), ControlNet keyframe; posts to /api/studio/run, brand presets from /api/studio/brand.

nodes.label: Subtitles Studio Page
nodes.rationale: Two-step flow: (1) erase burned-in captions with AI video inpainting that reconstructs the background per frame (/api/clean-subs, restorable via /api/clean-restore), (2) create and burn flicker-free word-timed subtitles over the erased band from the video's audio or the dub script (/api/run caption|recaption).

nodes.label: Power Tools Page
nodes.rationale: Persistent job table (jobs survive restarts) with Stop/Resume via /api/job/<id>/{stop,resume}, and the fal.ai spend ledger from /api/spend.

nodes.label: Transcript & Script Page
nodes.rationale: Verify what was said, then edit or AI-rewrite the script to be dubbed: transcribe via /api/run{transcribe}, edit via GET/POST /api/script/<stem>, free local Claude rewrite via /api/copywrite.

nodes.label: Video Studio Architecture Doc
nodes.rationale: Target: one local Flask app on localhost:5180 orchestrating existing engines via subprocess; chosen because the autoVSL/dashboard architecture is already proven, so add only a persistent job store, central config, and engine wrappers instead of reimplementing engines.

nodes.label: Video Studio Migration Plan
nodes.rationale: Six additive phases (scaffold -> resumable jobs -> engine wrappers -> DubSync Repair -> Library/Exports -> port-5180 cutover), all completed 2026-07-16, plus post-migration Visual Repair, Object Repair, Brand Studio and Clone Winner features; guiding principle: adopt what works, wrap what's risky, rebuild nothing; originals never modified so rollback is always possible.

nodes.label: Video Studio Project Inventory
nodes.rationale: Read-only survey (2026-07-16) of autoVSL dashboard (port 5170, migration base), subtitle-studio (port 5180, best erase engine), dubbing-studio (7860, XTTS/Wav2Lip); key insight: the unified app was ~80% already built inside autoVSL/dashboard; 8 of 11 required modules already existed, only DubSync Repair was net-new.

nodes.label: Video Studio Unified Brief
nodes.rationale: The source-of-truth requirements doc: one local-first Windows app at localhost:5180 with 11 target modules and the safe rule 'do not overwrite or delete Subtitle Studio or AutoVSL yet'.

nodes.label: Video Studio Flask Server (app/server.py)
nodes.rationale: Single Flask app on 127.0.0.1:5180, copied from autoVSL/dashboard/server.py and re-pathed through config.json; serves all tab pages and /api endpoints; one daemon thread per job so long subprocess work never blocks requests.

nodes.label: Persistent Resumable Job Manager
nodes.rationale: Replaces the in-memory jobs dict of both legacy apps: jobs/jobs.json index + per-job log, write-through on every transition so jobs survive restarts; dead running jobs become 'interrupted' with a Resume that re-invokes engines which pick up their own checkpoint caches (ProPainter chunk cache, whisper words.json) — safest resumability win, no engine changes.

nodes.label: GPU Lock / Arbitration
nodes.rationale: Single 4 GB GPU: every GPU engine goes through GPU_LOCK; runner also polls for a foreign erase from legacy apps and waits (ported from subtitle-studio) — never two GPU jobs at once or the card OOMs; _awake_keeper keeps Windows awake mid-job.

nodes.label: fal.ai Cost Gating & Spend Ledger
nodes.rationale: Money is always gated: no paid fal.ai action runs without confirm_cost; every spend is estimated up front (per-clip model price table $0.05-$0.40) and appended to output/fal_spend.json; the UI surfaces live $ estimates and a running spend badge.

nodes.label: Adopt-Don't-Rebuild Migration Principle
nodes.rationale: Video Studio = a copy of autoVSL/dashboard rebased into video-studio/, rebound to 5180, with subtitle-studio and dubbing-studio engines wired in as subprocess back-ends; keeps every proven engine in place, changes no source project, and both old apps stay runnable as fallbacks.

nodes.label: Separate Venvs via Subprocess
nodes.rationale: Dependency pins are load-bearing (torch==2.5.1, numpy<2, opencv==4.10.0.84, coqui-tts==0.25.1) so the four venvs are kept separate and called via subprocess; merging environments is explicitly deferred as too risky.

nodes.label: Subtitle Recovery Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Fully local, resumable flow: UI box/auto -> erase_subs.py (ProPainter, chunked with resume cache) -> backup original -> recaption.py (faster-whisper words.json -> lines.json -> ASS captions burned exactly over the erased band); subtitle-studio's engines preferred over the dashboard's copies for better detection and resume.

nodes.label: Dubbing & Lip-Sync Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Edit script -> local_dub.py (XTTS voice clone + synth, fit to length, normalize, mux) -> lipsync.py (Wav2Lip + GFPGAN/CodeFormer under GPU_LOCK) -> per-dub provenance record -> versioned takes; cloud path via fal.ai stays behind the cost gate.

nodes.label: DubSync Repair
nodes.rationale: The one net-new feature: fix a bad dub without re-cloning the voice by composing proven functions (re-sync via lipsync.py, re-fit via fit_audio_to_duration, re-normalize, re-mux); reads per-dub provenance to know what to re-run; repairs never touch final.mp4, each lands as a versioned take.

nodes.label: Ads Factory / VSL Build Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Product/research/banks -> build-vsl (Claude CLI, free) -> generate-vo (edge-tts, free) -> generate-video (fal.ai paid OR ComfyUI local free) -> assemble (ffmpeg); autoVSL scripts reused verbatim via subprocess.

nodes.label: Trash / Soft-Delete Restore System
nodes.rationale: Everything reversible: deletes move to .trash/ with index.json (multi-piece bundle delete of video + transcript + dub workdir), restorable via POST /api/trash/restore; originals never destroyed.

nodes.label: ProPainter Video Inpainting Engine
nodes.rationale: The quality subtitle-erase path (tools/ProPainter): AI video inpaint on GPU, auto caption-band detection (EasyOCR/CRAFT), 720-frame chunks, fp16, persistent resume cache — the resumability model Video Studio generalizes.

nodes.label: faster-whisper Transcription Engine
nodes.rationale: distil-large-v3 with word timestamps cached in words.json (course_pipeline/.venv); powers transcription, editable lines.json, and word-timed ASS caption burning.

nodes.label: Coqui XTTS v2 Voice Clone Engine
nodes.rationale: Local free voice clone + synthesis (17 languages), time-stretched to video length pitch-preserved, normalized to -16 LUFS; from dubbing-studio.
nodes.norm_label: coqui xtts v2 voice clone engine

nodes.label: Wav2Lip Lip-Sync Engine
nodes.rationale: Local Wav2Lip GAN + GFPGAN v1.4 or CodeFormer face restore (weights in tools/Wav2Lip and CodeFormer/); the local lip-sync chain behind dubbing and DubSync Repair.

nodes.label: fal.ai Cloud Generation Service
nodes.rationale: Paid cloud path for video generation (seedance/wan/hailuo/kling) and voice-clone/lip-sync (f5-tts, LatentSync); FAL_KEY lives only in autoVSL/.env, injected into subprocess env — single secret location.

nodes.label: ComfyUI Local Generation Service
nodes.rationale: Local free GPU image/video generation at 127.0.0.1:8188 (SD 1.5, Real-ESRGAN, ControlNet); the $0 alternative to fal.ai.

nodes.label: Claude CLI Local AI
nodes.rationale: ~/.local/bin/claude.exe used as free local AI for VSL building, copywriting/rewrite, caption spell-fix, and vision-based QC review — runs on the Claude subscription, no API cost.

nodes.label: VSR Magic Erase Tool (video-subtitle-remover)
nodes.rationale: tools/vsr: STTN-based inpainting subtitle remover (~5 fps), the 'magic erase' alternative engine invoked by subtitle-studio.

nodes.label: liitt Brand Kit (banks/liitt-brand-kit.json)
nodes.rationale: Brand presets, style suffix (editorial mystic, indigo/gold Glow palette) and negative prompt that the ComfyUI Studio applies to keep generated creatives on-brand for liitt/Fairy Flame.

nodes.label: STTN: Spatial-Temporal Transformer Networks for Video Inpainting
nodes.author: Y. Zeng, J. Fu, H. Chao
nodes.rationale: Formulates video inpainting as multi-to-multi: fill holes in all input frames simultaneously using multi-scale patch-based multi-head attention (frame-level encoder -> stacked spatial-temporal transformers -> frame-level decoder) plus a spatial-temporal adversarial loss; motivated by prior attention methods assuming global affine motion and lacking temporal-coherence optimization; beats SOTA by 2.4% PSNR / 19.7% VFID.
nodes.norm_label: sttn: spatial-temporal transformer networks for video inpainting

nodes.label: Video Inpainting Intro/Survey Deck
nodes.rationale: Design-notes deck (largely CJK) surveying video inpainting approaches behind the VSR tool: flow/mask methods, 3D-CNN/RNN blocks, gated convolution, region normalization, memory search+read attention, OPN, RNoT, STTN, and a LogoLoss for logo/watermark removal (TikTok use case).

nodes.label: OPN: Onion Peel Networks for Deep Video Completion (ICCV 2019)
nodes.rationale: Fills missing regions step-by-step from boundary inward with pixel-wise attention over encoder query/key/value features; a key predecessor discussed in the deck and in the STTN paper's related work.
nodes.norm_label: opn: onion peel networks for deep video completion (iccv 2019)

nodes.label: Region Normalization (RNoT)
nodes.rationale: Normalization scheme applied per known/unknown region (RN-B in encoder, RN-L in decoder with Res-Blocks) improving inpainting decoders; presented in the deck as an OPN enhancement.

nodes.label: LogoLoss for Logo Removal
nodes.rationale: Loss term discussed in the deck for training inpainting to remove logos/watermarks — directly relevant to the subtitle/watermark erase use case of the VSR tool.

nodes.label: Video Inpainting
nodes.rationale: Reconstructing masked video regions spatially and temporally coherently (vs per-frame image inpainting); the core technique that makes 'erase burned-in subtitles and recover the true background' possible in both ProPainter and STTN/VSR paths.
